channel.title: Compiler From Scratch (2025 Archive) on Polyscone
channel.description: Recent content in Compiler From Scratch (2025 Archive) on Polyscone

item.title: Building a Scanner
item.description: Start the Fyn compiler in Go by defining source files and tokens, then scanning keywords, identifiers, integers, punctuation, and source locations.

item.title: Building a Pratt Parser
item.description: Build a precedence-aware Pratt parser that turns Fyn expressions into an AST while supporting prefix, infix, and postfix operators with configurable associativity.

item.title: Building Parser Test Infrastructure
item.description: Create readable AST snapshots and source-embedded parser fixtures using trivia, node spans, tree walking, and automated expected-output comparisons.

item.title: Parsing Functions and Improving Parser Errors
item.description: Strengthen parser tests and diagnostics, then add module, function-declaration, and block nodes with error recovery and AST support.

item.title: Building a Type Checker
item.description: Parse function return types and return statements, then build an interned type system and annotate expression nodes with checked types.

item.title: Type-Checking Return Statements
item.description: Add function types and lexical environments, resolve built-in type names, and validate return counts and expression types inside functions.

item.title: Generating Basic IR
item.description: Design a linear intermediate representation and recursively lower typed Fyn functions, constants, returns, and binary expressions into readable IR.

item.title: Intel SDM, Vol 1, Basic Execution Environment and Procedures
item.description: Study the Intel Software Developer's Manual to understand notation, operating modes, registers, memory addressing, procedures, and core integer instructions before writing the backend.

item.title: Intel SDM Vol 2, Instruction Format and Encoding
item.description: Read Intel's instruction-format reference to learn prefixes, opcodes, ModR/M, SIB, REX, displacements, immediates, and the notation used by instruction tables.

item.title: Encoding Register-to-Register MOV
item.description: Start the x86-64 encoder with register operands and implement tested register-to-register MOV encoding using operand-size, ModR/M, and REX fields.

item.title: Encoding Register/Memory MOV
item.description: Extend MOV encoding to register-to-memory and memory-to-register operations, including the special RSP/R12 SIB and RBP/R13 displacement forms.

item.title: Encoding Memory Displacements
item.description: Encode base-plus-displacement and RIP-relative MOV operands while selecting compact disp8 forms and handling base-pointer exceptions.

item.title: Encoding Scaled-Index Addressing
item.description: Implement SIB encoding for scaled-index effective addresses, including scale conversion, REX extensions, missing-base forms, and special stack/base registers.

item.title: Encoding Immediate MOV
item.description: Add immediate-source MOV forms for register and memory destinations using opcode-register extensions, /digit fields, REX rules, and width-aware immediates.

item.title: Improving x86-64 Encoder Tests
item.description: Add encoder assertions and replace repetitive hand-written cases with a compact instruction parser that derives operands, sizes, registers, immediates, and memory addresses.

item.title: Encoding LEA, ADD, and SUB
item.description: Grow the encoder beyond MOV by implementing LEA and shared ADD/SUB forms for registers, memory, immediates, and accumulator-specific opcodes.

item.title: Encoding MUL, DIV, and RET
item.description: Complete the initial instruction set with sign-extended ADD/SUB immediates, implicit-register MUL/DIV forms, and the single-byte RET instruction.

item.title: Lowering IR to x86-64 Machine Code
item.description: Connect the IR and x86-64 encoder with naive virtual-register allocation, operand conversion, instruction dispatch, and end-to-end disassembly.

item.title: Writing PE32+ Executables
item.description: Write a PE32+ image generator from the Windows specification, emit headers and sections, inspect the binary, and run generated x86-64 code as a native executable.
